# What ships, and what each part is

*Generated by `scripts/render-shipped-map.mjs` from the publisher's own allowlist.
Do not edit by hand — re-run it instead. 208 files, 2.34 MB.*

You have just cloned [`bhparsons/redline`](https://github.com/bhparsons/redline).
This is what is in it.

## The shape of the thing

Three pieces, and the split between them is the whole design:

- **The extension is the UI.** It shows you the document and captures what you say about it.
- **The runner is the trust layer.** It is the only thing that writes your files, and it
  validates every change before it touches disk.
- **Your agent session does the thinking.** It reads the document, writes the prose, and asks
  the runner to apply it. It never writes to disk itself.

That last line is why an agent cannot corrupt your document by being wrong about markup: it
does not have the pen. Everything below is one of those three, or something that supports them.

## Directory by directory

### `runner/` — The trust layer — 51 files

Everything that writes. The runner serves your document over HTTP, holds the
comment sidecar, applies edits, validates them, snapshots them for undo, and
records every run. **It is the only thing that writes your files** — the
browser never does, and neither does any agent.

Start at `runner/index.mjs` (the process) and `runner/lib/api.mjs` (every
endpoint). The rules that cannot be bypassed live in `runner/lib/surgery.mjs`:
edits are targeted string replacements on the raw source, never a DOM
re-serialisation, because re-serialising decodes entities and reformats markup
across the whole file. `runner/lib/store.mjs` is the sidecar,
`runner/lib/scope.mjs` the guardrail that pauses a change reaching wider than
the comment that asked for it, and `runner/lib/watch-session.mjs` the
bookkeeping behind the live watcher loop.

`runner/skills/` is a different kind of "skill" from the top-level one: these
are context packs loaded into a revision prompt, not agent instructions.

### `extension/` — The UI — 22 files

A Chrome extension, and only a UI. It injects the review overlay into a page the
runner is serving, captures your selection and your comment, and shows the
thread. It asks the runner to do things; it never edits the document itself.

`extension/overlay.js` is the whole review surface. `extension/popup.*` is the
status dashboard — runner version, extension version, last run — and comparing
those two version numbers is the fastest way to explain "it stopped working".

### `bin/` — The command line — 1 file

`bin/redline.mjs` is the single entry point: `serve`, `demo`, `instrument`,
`install-mcp`, and the agent verbs. It finds or starts a runner and gets out of
the way.

### `docs/` — The contracts — 5 files

`AGENT-CONTRACT.md` is normative: every endpoint, every payload, and the watch
protocol. `AGENT-USAGE.md` is worked examples. If an agent and this repo ever
disagree, the contract wins.

### `skills/` — The Claude Code skill — 1 file

`redline-watch` teaches a session to attach to a document and act on comments as
they arrive. Symlink it into `~/.claude/skills/` — a copy works too, but a
symlink tracks updates.

### `examples/` — A worked agent, in plain Node — 1 file

`watch-collaborate.mjs` implements the watch protocol with no dependencies and
no MCP. Read it if you are wiring up an agent that is not Claude Code, or if you
want to see what the MCP tools do underneath.

### `samples/` — Fixture documents — 4 files

What `redline demo` seeds from, plus the teaching thread that arrives beside it
— four comments demonstrating an edit request, a note, an open question and a
decline.

### `test/` — The evidence — 114 files

The suite, run with `node test.mjs`. It ships because a suite you can run is
worth more than a claim that one exists — and because when something breaks for
you, a failing test here is the fastest thing to send back.

### `test.mjs` — The suite entry point

`node test.mjs`, or `--fast` for the same thing.

### `report.mjs` — The shareable report

Renders a document's comment history into one self-contained HTML file — every
comment, how it was resolved, before/after diffs, and what each run cost. Read
only: it touches neither the document nor the sidecar.

### `scripts/` — Packaging — 1 file

`package-extension.mjs` zips the extension for distribution.

### `.github/` — Reporting a problem — 2 files

The issue template. It asks for four things, versions first: a stale extension
against a newer runner is the most common cause of "it stopped working" and is
invisible unless the two numbers are compared.

### `README.md` — Start here

Install once, then work from your own repo.

### `package.json` — The manifest

Rewritten on the way out of the private repo, so it describes the published package.

### `.gitignore` — Ignores

Chiefly `.history/` (undo snapshots) and `*.review.json` if you would rather not commit review threads.

### `LICENSE` — MIT

## What is NOT here, and why

This repo is generated from a larger private one by an allowlist, so the absence of something
is deliberate rather than accidental. The design record, the planning documents, the board
process and the maintainer tooling stay behind. Nothing that is missing is needed to run,
read, or extend what is here.

## Where to start reading

| If you want to | Read |
|---|---|
| use it | `README.md` |
| wire up your own agent | `docs/AGENT-CONTRACT.md`, then `examples/watch-collaborate.mjs` |
| understand the write path | `runner/lib/api.mjs` → `runner/lib/apply.mjs` → `runner/lib/surgery.mjs` |
| understand the live watcher | `runner/lib/watch-session.mjs` |
| change the UI | `extension/overlay.js` |
| trust any of it | `node test.mjs` |
